A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SD-KDE and retain the same core algorithm, theorem and original experiments. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian/Laplace mixture experiments, 2D density-estimation results and MNIST image-density rankings in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds empirical-score comparisons and iterative SD-KDE experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 remains unchanged, but v2 adds Emp-SD-KDE, which obtains scores from Silverman KDE, and an iterative procedure that recomputes scores and repeatedly corrects samples with decaying step sizes (Sections 3.1 and 3.3). This substantially extends the original single-step procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 1D Gaussian/Laplace mixtures, 2D spirals and Gaussian mixtures, and MNIST image-density rankings. The additional studies remain within these data families and tasks; their differences concern score estimation, mixture parameters and iteration settings.

E2.justification: Silverman KDE remains the benchmark comparator, and retained experiments preserve their comparison methods. The new empirical-score and iterative curves evaluate extensions of SD-KDE itself rather than introducing another competing density estimator.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed-bandwidth iteration experiments and KL divergence alongside MISE. The Gaussian study specifies 1,000 samples and bandwidth 0.15; existing experiment settings remain unchanged. The new Laplace experiment has an unresolved sample-count inconsistency: Figure 14's legend says 750, while its caption says 1,000.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining additive-score-noise and seed-consistency analyses, v2 tests KDE-estimated versus oracle scores and sensitivity to repeated corrections. Figures 7 and 14 examine density, score, KL and MISE trajectories, adding substantial evidence about early improvements and subsequent over-correction.

E5.justification: Figures 7 and 14 newly report Monte Carlo MISE over 200 replicates and display error bars, although the bars' statistical meaning is unspecified. Existing 50-seed reporting remains unchanged; this does not establish increased replication of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds Emp-SD-KDE convergence slopes of -0.73, -0.40 and -0.88, compared with Silverman slopes of -0.54, -0.36 and -0.63 under the corresponding settings. Figures 7 and 14 add nonmonotonic KL/MISE trajectories across iterations. Matched original results are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds Corollary 1, expressing leading bias through score-estimation error and its derivative. The original exact-score theorem, bandwidth selection, convergence rate and proof are otherwise retained; moving the proof from Appendix A to Section 4 is organizational.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of score-based debiasing, improved asymptotic MISE convergence and effectiveness with noisy scores. The added abstract phrase about improving convergence restates a claim already explicit in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of iterative correction as removing residual bias, with diminishing returns and eventual over-correction discussed in the figure captions. Its limitations paragraph newly emphasizes score-estimation costs while reiterating the existing exact-score requirement for the main guarantee.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses cluster and Apple M2 hardware, memory, CUDA 12.5 and runtime information. It also specifies the iterative method's bandwidth and correction-scale schedule. The original DDPM architecture and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to higher-order kernels, Langevin dynamics and score-/sample-based density estimation are retained. The related discussion moves from Appendix B to Section 5 without changing its research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: the proof and additional discussion become main Sections 4 and 5, the conclusion moves to Section 6, and experimental appendices are regrouped. Empirical-score, iteration and limitations passages are added, although much original prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds two explanatory schematics, an empirical-score comparison and two iterative-analysis figures. All eleven original figures are retained but rearranged and renumbered; Table 1 moves into the main text, and title, headings and figure placement are reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical evidence through KDE-estimated scores and iteration studies, supported by a score-error corollary and added reproducibility details. However, Section 3.3 suggests improvement with each iteration despite reversals in Figures 7 and 14, and Figure 14 contradicts its caption on sample count. These reporting problems limit the gains, but the additional evidence and transparency provide a modest net improvement.
